objects.name: Subject Dies by Suicide
objects.description:
Summary: Activity has the assessed impact of contributing to the subject's death by suicide.

Detail: This impact records that the subject died by suicide, and that an analyst assesses the activity to have contributed to that outcome.

One example of activity which brings about death by suicide is sextortion, in which an actor obtains a subject's intimate imagery and then demands payment under threat of distribution. Cases have been documented where the gap between first contact and the target's death by suicide is just a few hours. Sustained harassment campaigns produce the same outcome over much longer periods.

Example

Jordan DeMay, a seventeen-year-old in Michigan, was contacted on Instagram in March 2022 by an account posing as a young woman. The account was a hacked Instagram profile purchased by Samuel and Samson Ogoshi. [They obtained an intimate image from him, demanded 1,000 US dollars, and threatened to publish it.](https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2024/09/06/sextortion-samuel-samson-ogoshi-jordan-demay/) He died by suicide hours later. [The actors pleaded guilty in April 2024 to conspiracy to sexually exploit minors, and were each sentenced to seventeen and a half years in prison.](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/two-nigerians-sentenced-years-sextortion-case-led-michigan-teens-rcna169730)

The case demonstrates an organised group of actors using purchased hacked accounts bringing about an impact not part of their original objectives; the suicide of their target.

Hana Kimura, a 22-year-old Japanese professional wrestler and cast member of the reality series Terrace House, was found dead on 23 May 2020. [Notes left at her home cited the volume of abusive messages she had been receiving on social media,](https://unfpa.org/node/42344) which followed an on-screen argument with another cast member after he had accidentally ruined one of her wrestling costumes while doing his own laundry. [Two men who had posted insults about her online were fined 9,000 yen each,](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/japan-online-insults-jail-cyberbullying-reality-star-death-rcna33669) close to the maximum then available under Japan's insult law, which capped penalties at under 30 days' detention or a fine of under 10,000 yen. Her mother, Kyoko Kimura, campaigned on the inadequacy of those penalties, and on 13 June 2022 Japan's Diet [passed a law raising the maximum punishment for insult to one year's imprisonment or a fine of 300,000 yen,](https://edition.cnn.com/2022/06/14/asia/japan-cyberbullying-law-intl-hnk-scli) with a provision requiring the law to be reviewed within three years of taking effect for its impact on freedom of expression.
